The Snake That Eats Puzzle Game Mechanics

A collection of single-screen Puzzlescript games, designed by members of the Thinky Puzzle Games Discord community, from January to July 2026.

Games are presented in the order they were made, not in order of difficulty, so feel free to play them in any order you like!

Controls:

  • Z is undo
  • R is restart
  • WASD or arrow keys for movement (swipe on mobile)
  • X or Spacebar for action (tap on mobile)
  • ESC exits to the level select

Participants in this collaboration were given a small piece of the previous participant's puzzle (either the sprites, or the shape of the level*) and tasked with using it to create a brand new puzzle.

*because we were experimenting with the format, there are two puzzles that also use the same mechanics as the previous puzzle: Mining Caverns and Closed Circuit

M0liusX45 days ago (3 edits) (+3)

That first level "Metal Gear Liquid 3: Snake Feeder" was pretty gnarly, ngl. But it was doable after a couple of hours at hammering away. My one hint to players struggling is to notice that the snake will always take a step towards a shortest path to where you land after you move. So if you want them to take a specific path, consider where the snake and you have to be placed for that decision to be a shortest path. Figuring out the routes you can take to maintain your gap with the snake and increasing it with the apples is pretty much key. There are a couple other brain blast moments, and out of the box thinking, but I will not spoil the fun.
I also really enjoyed the two fish levels at the end. Really awesome game guys!

okayseas47 days ago(+2)

confirming that after a few days of revisiting, i have finally beaten the second level. I thought for sure, at first, it was impossible. I stumbled upon the first move - confusing the snake's pathfinding and letting it commit a disadvantageous path. From there, I worked out blocking with the barrels for a long long time until I finally discovered a configuration that let me freely solve the remainder of the puzzle.

Pretty difficult puzzle but super nice to solve - no hidden mechanics, just challenge your assumptions and consider where the computer would make a mistake in good faith. The snake does not read bombs as obstacles.
